title: India Semiconductor Fab Expansion 2026: Tata PSMC Plant Timeline, Investments & Job Impact
content:
India’s semiconductor ecosystem reaches a historic milestone as commercial fabrication facilities in Dholera (Gujarat) and advanced packaging plants in Morigaon (Assam) prepare for commercial silicon production under the ₹1.26 Lakh Crore ($15.2 Billion) Indian Semiconductor Mission.

🔥 Live Policy Signal: Government confirms pari-passu financial support covering 50% of project costs for approved semiconductor fabs.

⚡ Quick Answer: Executive Summary

India’s ₹1.26 Lakh Crore semiconductor expansion includes Tata Electronics’ 28nm–40nm commercial fab in Dholera, Gujarat (50,000 monthly wafer starts), Micron’s packaging unit in Sanand, and CG Power-Renesas OSAT facility in Assam. The first commercial silicon wafers are scheduled for market delivery in Q4 2026, generating over 100,000 direct and indirect engineering jobs.

What Happened: Government Accelerates Silicon Roadmap

The Union Cabinet, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Minister for Electronics and IT Ashwini Vaishnaw, has accelerated execution phases for India’s foundational semiconductor manufacturing clusters under the Indian Semiconductor Mission (ISM).

With a cumulative capital outlay exceeding ₹1,26,000 Crore ($15.2 Billion), construction and cleanroom installation work at the anchor fabrication unit in Dholera Special Investment Region (SIR), Gujarat, and the assembly-testing plant in Morigaon, Assam, have entered advanced hardware commissioning stages.

Commercial production of 28-nanometer (nm), 40nm, and 90nm legacy node microchips is scheduled to commence commercial distribution by late 2026, targeting power management integrated circuits (PMICs), display drivers, automotive microcontrollers, and IoT hardware modules.

Why This Is Trending: Global Tech & Supply Chain Shift

The global technology sector is closely monitoring India’s transition from a fabless design leader into a physical silicon manufacturing country. Search interest across industry indexing has surged by +210% for semiconductor supply chain queries in India. The urgency stems from three core drivers:

  1. Global Supply Chain Diversification: Electronics conglomerates are actively establishing alternatives to concentrated manufacturing centers in Taiwan and East Asia.
  2. Surging Domestic Electronics Demand: India’s domestic electronics market is projected to reach $300 Billion by 2026, consuming over $64 Billion worth of semiconductors annually.
  3. Unprecedented Fiscal Support: The Central Government and State Governments are providing up to 50% capital subsidy on a pari-passu basis, drastically lowering capital expenditure barriers for global tech consortiums.

Key Details: Infrastructure & Investment Breakdown

The table below outlines the core semiconductor projects currently underway across India under ISM Phase-1 and Phase-2 outlays:

Facility Location Primary Consortium Facility Type Project Capex Planned Capacity Target Rollout
Dholera (Gujarat) Tata Electronics & PSMC (Taiwan) 28nm, 40nm Fab ₹91,000 Cr ($11B) 50,000 Wafers / Mo Q4 2026
Morigaon (Assam) Tata Semiconductor Assembly (TSAT) Advanced OSAT ₹27,000 Cr ($3.25B) 48M Chips / Day Q3 2026
Sanand (Gujarat) CG Power, Renesas & Stars Micro Automotive OSAT ₹7,600 Cr ($915M) 15M Chips / Day Late 2026
Sanand (Gujarat) Micron Technology (USA) DRAM / NAND Packaging ₹22,500 Cr ($2.75B) Module Packaging Operational

Background: India’s Transition from Fabless Design to Commercial Fabs

For decades, India maintained a world-class semiconductor design ecosystem—housing over 20,000 chip design engineers working for Qualcomm, Intel, Nvidia, and Texas Instruments—yet lacked commercial fabrication foundries.

In December 2021, the Cabinet approved the landmark ₹76,000 Crore ($10 Billion) Incentive Scheme for Semiconductors and Display Manufacturing. Following strong international response and consortium proposals, total government capital backing was subsequently expanded beyond ₹1.2 Lakh Crore.

What This Means for Readers, Industry, and Investors

  • For Indian Manufacturers & OEMs: Local availability of power management ICs and microcontrollers will reduce component lead times from months to days, shielding electronics makers from global supply bottlenecks.
  • For Engineers & Graduates: Creating an estimated 20,000 direct high-tech engineering jobs and over 80,000 indirect technical roles across materials science, chemical processing, and cleanroom management.
  • For Global Investors: Demonstrates India’s capacity to execute complex, multi-billion-dollar greenfield industrial infrastructure with single-window regulatory clearances and guaranteed grid allocations.

What Happens Next

  • Q3 2026: Initial pilot testing and machinery trial runs at Tata's Morigaon packaging facility in Assam.
  • Q4 2026: First commercial silicon wafer fabrication trial batches at Dholera Fab unit.
  • 2027 Onward: Expected announcement of ISM Phase-3, focusing on sub-14nm advanced nodes and compound semiconductors for EV powertrains.

faq.question: What types of microchips will be manufactured at the Dholera Fab?
faq.answer: The Dholera facility will produce 28nm, 40nm, 55nm, and 90nm planar silicon chips. These mature nodes are vital for automotive control units, mobile power management ICs, smart meters, industrial automation controllers, and consumer electronics.

faq.question: How much financial subsidy does the Indian government provide?
faq.answer: Under the Indian Semiconductor Mission, the Union Government provides a 50% financial subsidy on total capital expenditure on a pari-passu basis. Host state governments (such as Gujarat and Assam) provide additional top-up incentives and land concessions.

faq.question: When will commercial chips made in India hit the market?
faq.answer: Initial commercial wafer fabrication and chip packaging outputs from Morigaon (Assam) and Dholera (Gujarat) are scheduled to enter commercial supply chains in late 2026, with full volumetric scaling through 2027.

faq.question: Who is Tata Electronics' foreign technology partner?
faq.answer: Tata Electronics has partnered with Taiwan’s Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp (PSMC). PSMC provides proven process technology transfer, foundry operational expertise, and cleanroom architecture design for the Dholera fab.

faq.question: How many jobs will the semiconductor expansion create in India?
faq.answer: The combined semiconductor projects in Dholera, Sanand, and Morigaon are projected to create over 20,000 direct specialized engineering jobs and 80,000+ indirect employment opportunities across supply chain and logistics sectors.
